subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should clean empty assistant output be treated as successful silent output for all isolated cron agent runs in both CLI and embedded runner paths?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but it changes upgrade semantics for cron jobs that currently surface `empty_response` as a failure signal, including delivered cron jobs.

options.title: Accept all-cron silent success
options.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix and make clean empty assistant output an `ok` silent result for isolated cron runs in both runner paths.

options.title: Require gated silence
options.body: Ask for a revision that only sets the flag for no-deliver, explicit silent, or per-job opted-in cron runs, with default-failure and opt-in-success tests.

options.title: Choose another canonical branch
options.body: Pause this PR only if maintainers sponsor a different open fix candidate as the landing path for the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix and make clean empty assistant output an `ok` silent result for isolated cron runs in both runner paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice centers on cron executor policy and runner handoff behavior, where recent cron runtime history points most strongly to this owner route.
